key_insight: LLM agents can recover hidden circuit behavior from pin-level experiments, but reliable reconstruction and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.
engineering_relevance: ChiProgramBench tests whether agents can turn experimental observations of stateful hardware into functionally correct, resource-efficient gate-level replacements.
method: Probe hidden simulated circuits through their input and output pins across 18 hardware tasks.
Compare black-box discovery with function-guided reconstruction that reveals circuit purpose and pin roles.
Submit netlists using public library cells; evaluate cycle-by-cycle correctness before awarding power, delay, and area credit.
evidence_signal: Across 432 trials of 6 agent configurations, full-pass rates were 12.0% for black-box and 14.8% for function-guided tasks; only 3 of 58 fully passing designs improved combined power, area, and delay over the reference.
watch_item: Results cover 18 simulated tasks; passing hidden tests does not establish correctness for every possible input sequence.
paper_title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
